Quick start: do this first

How does this work? In short: you gather your attention, you notice something, you do one thing in response, you wait, and you come all the way back out again. It’s a lot like playing or falling in love, or becoming curious, or gaining confidence. Nothing dramatic needs to happen.

Before you do your first session, read through the induction and full return while you’re awake. Find a time and a place where you will be physically secure for this time. Decide on one purpose for this session. Notice what you’re leaving alone for today. Put the screen aside and do the work.

5. Closure: When you notice that something is happening for you (a sensation, image, phrase, feeling, objection, or even a deepening silence), gently respond to the next thing that is offered to you (this may be a need to offer yourself warmth, to establish a boundary, to follow a direction, to simply listen for a while longer, etc) until you feel the experience move to completion and you can return fully to yourself and this room together. If you feel moved to note something or to take action in the real world in response to your experience, please do so now.

*NOTE: If at any point you feel yourself becoming panicky, disoriented, unreal, or unable to function, move to closure. This is distinct from choosing to engage deeply with a difficult feeling while remaining present.

Do you usually think in words?

Before you pick a script, notice whether you have an inner voice. Do you notice words or phrases in your head, not spoken out loud, when you are thinking to yourself? All the time? Sometimes? Rarely? Almost never? (Note that the words do not have to be spoken aloud in your head. Just notice whether you use words when you think.) Does this vary depending on what kind of thinking you’re doing? Can you choose to think in words silently to yourself, even if you don’t usually do this?

This is different from noticing that in a particular situation, you notice feelings first and words later. It’s ok to say that you’re not sure; the point of these questions is to help you pick a way of doing this that will work for you, not to diagnose you.

If you don’t think in words, please read “say” and “ask” and “listen” in this guide as suggestions, not commands. You may want to say things out loud, or write them down, or use a recording, or just do the suggestion without wording it first. Also, do not assume that the child or protector needs to say things back to you in complete sentences. Nor does it mean that you will necessarily get an image instead; try things out and see what works.

De-hypnosis: wake up inside the influence

One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is an increased awareness of all the ways you’re being manipulated in your day-to-day life. By a screen? By a specific ad? By a politician? By a religion? By erotic imprinting? By an authority figure? By the desire for belonging? By shame? By a sense of urgency? By repetition? It’s all around you. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.

Some common ways you may know you’re being manipulated include a sense of urgency, a sense of specialness, FOMO, being made to feel like you won’t be included if you don’t go along, sexual charge, shame, being confused, a fantasy of being rescued, a sense of destiny, a sense that you should obey, a sense of secret knowledge, or an excessive sense of certainty about something pretty quickly.

If you’re being hypnotically influenced, stop. Don’t listen. Don’t rebel, either, just stop and realize that you’re being influenced.

Some common ways hypnotic language becomes manipulative includes:

“you’ll realize, eventually, that…” “you may eventually admit that…” “the reason you’re not feeling it yet is…” “even if part of you doesn’t feel that’s true…” “your higher self knows…” “everyone knows…” “the reason you don’t believe that’s true is your ego’s fear of…”

Other language patterns to watch out for include:

What’s being claimed here? What’s the inevitable choice being framed for me here? What’s being presupposed? Who benefits from framing it this way? What’s the emotionally charged bit? What’s not being said? What do I need to say in order to opt out of the frame, and is it safe for me to do so (will I suffer negative consequences – physical, social, financial, reputational, spiritual etc – if I say no)?

The above is a rough guide to help bring more of the ‘adult’ into the conversation. Use more of the above when the state is more powerful.

Soft language can still take away choice

These words in and of themselves are not coercive but, when used, can be part of coercion. Look for:

Saying something indirectly so that the listener’s conscious mind doesn’t get the chance to consider and reject it. This can be very specific, or it can be vague, casual or suggestive.

Using the mechanics of induction to focus the listener’s attention while seeming to be just explaining something (even about “anti-hypnosis”).

Treating any response (including “yes,” “no,” noticing, not noticing, resisting, or silence) as compliance.

Using “whether you notice it or not” to bind.

Using identity or ownership, such as suggesting that being safe or being good is a matter of obedience, or of taking on a particular role, or of being approved of by the guide, or of belonging to someone else.

Is there unannounced fractionation – coming in and out of absorption and back in again?

Does it covertly use post hypnosis cues (words, gestures, blinks, sounds or listening to it again) to try and make you do something later?

Does it use amnesia or exaggerating the truth about things like dreamstates, memory loss, imagery and body sensations?

Does the end of the recording leave you in some kind of role, with decreased judgement, impaired movements, make you blank or leave you in a non normal state for an indefinite period of time?

If at any point during a hypnosis you have a REAL choice to NOT carry on, turn it into a lighter hypnosis, use a different method, stay in full awareness, pause or stop the hypnosis then it can not be a covert hypnosis. “No” means no, even if someone with a nice voice is telling you to do something! If you are unsure that you can or can’t then you probably can’t. Simply not knowing your options isn’t a choice.

See appendix C for the longer version of how to check for de-hypnosis.

Appendix A: How to ask the subconscious a useful question

Your subconscious is not an AI but some things are transferable. You need to make sure that prompt engineering serves you to be more present, more honest, more loving and hear the messages of your subconscious better.

The following elements can be relevant for prompt engineering when you need to be more precise:

Role: Who is it that you talk to

Context: Which situation is it

Intention: What do you want to achieve

Constraint: What constraints do you want to set to make it more safe or to be more precise (like do not force things, be truthful, be loving etc.)

Output: Which kind of output is most helpful for you? Images, words, signals in your body, memories, next actions, questions, symbols etc. Or sometimes it is best to simply rest.

Evaluation: How will you know if you got a good answer? Criteria like is it true, kind, timely, brings stability, specific, testable etc.

Iteration: Change the prompt depending on the feedback you get from life

In some prompts it is good to include that it is safe for the system to not give an answer. Otherwise your analytical brain will feel like it needs to come up with something and distort things.

And if the system realizes that it needs more time to process or it is most helpful to not give an answer, then the system can deepen the comfortable rest in the body and give a nice silence as an answer. It is completely fine and a successful run if the answer is silence.

Sometimes there is simply nothing going on or the answer is that it is not the right time and you should rest and build up capacity or do the obvious things you know you need to do.

Please show me the capacity first and then show me the content.

What are you protecting me from and what can I do so that you can trust me 1% more?

Prompt to decondition and get good intuition:

Here’s a simple prompt: Dear subconscious, as I bring this signal to mind, please disempower the parts that are conditioned. Which may come from my family of origin, religious indoctrination, marketing and advertising, erotic imprinting, political tribalism, trauma response or childhood survival conditioning. Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

Note: Using an induction will help your focus, making it easier to tap into the more esoteric parts of this work. That said, you don’t need to go into a trance state, play asleep, or give up your power to anyone. If you’re sober and distracted, or too analytical or guarded to easily reach the parts of you that need this work, it may be helpful to use an actual induction. However, if you’ve already gone into a trancey state through meditation or loveyhuasca or lucid dreaming, or you are freshly grieving or have been deeply moved by music or prayer or you are simply sleep deprived, you may want to skip ahead to the orientation and containment sections.

A note on how deep of a trance you need to go into for this work:

What an induction is actually doing

There is a real benefit to preparing a session before you start and once you've gathered your subject's attention you can deepen if necessary but you're free to start wording up if the context of the session requires it. You can use a number of ways to organise your subject's attention, counting is but one and if you're going to use it then say so. You can use conversation, stories, movement, repeated sounds, or simply curiosity etc... But if you're going to use them say so. Elegence is always useful, but not at the expense of doing something that you shouldn't be doing.

Also, with a simple enough target, why not try it first and if it works then deepen.

Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Client is king so you need to pick one purpose for the induction, one starting place, anchor or image, and one way to get back. Then you can bring in any of the other ingredients you want, but in a conscious way. If you feel the need to switch metaphors, do so consciously. You may want to bring in some feelings of warmth, or of setting boundaries, or of direction, or of being a neutral witness. You may want to use floating, stairs, gardens, going to an inner room, colored lights, talking to your inner child. It doesn't all have to be used.

You don't even need to use imagery. You can use any sense, rhythm, body movement, words, spatial sense, intuitive knowledge, or even no response at all to create the signal. Just be sure to use your chosen world when counting and when coming out of the induction. You can borrow qualities from other worlds, just be sure you don't borrow them into your own identity.

Start simple. Choose one verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one way of transitioning. Read your script out loud - it's easy to get carried away writing long, elegant sentences that turn into soup when you start the induction.

Before you begin

Read through the induction and Come all the way back to orient yourself to what will happen. Then decide what you want to explore, what you want to leave alone, and how much time you have. You may want to do the exercise for positive purposes such as stimulating love, play, confidence, creativity, or communion. Plan to allow a few minutes at the end for returning and reflecting on the experience.

Make sure you are in a safe place. Don't do this exercise if you are driving, near water, working with machinery, or taking care of others. Don't do this exercise if you are under the influence of alcohol or drugs, acutely confused, or otherwise not able to take care of yourself. (The only exception is the exercise later in this section entitled "Already open?" which is designed to help orient you.)

Decide how direct you want to be encouraged to go into a hypnotic state. Read through the script to find out what is going to happen, including the fact that your eyes will be asked to close and that you may be asked to come out of the hypnotic state and then go back in again. If you are using an audio recording, it's best to read the script ahead of time. Remind yourself that you can end the exercise at any time by saying "stop" (or "less" if you want less demand to go into the hypnotic state or "quiet" if you want the talking to stop), or by opening your eyes and ending the exercise. No part of you has to give permission for you to end the exercise.

Until you are confident about how to get in and out, it is wise to rehearse the skill in a context where you do not require the maximum effort that difficult subjects demand. Once the skill is easier to apply, you can relax into using it effortlessly. It is the lack of effort that produces the maximum benefit. Saying no is enough. You don’t have to say anything.

Develop the next part of your induction from what your subject is responding to, not what you intended. This principle of utilization means that whatever happens can be developed. If nothing happens, then nothing has happened. You don’t have to pretend that something has. The subject needs to know they are safe and how to leave the experience. The language skills that facilitate these are described in Appendix B and used in Let the next response guide you .

Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Practise reading this slowly into a recorder, or reading it aloud, or if you can learn it and use silent words. There’s time to do this.

It might be that a thought about something that’s happened during the day is still with you, or perhaps there’s a thought about doing this properly. Whatever is there, can you find it in yourself to turn your attention back to the anchor, even if there is a thought there?

and when you do come back, perhaps there was something of interest to you in all of this

Perhaps you can give yourself the time that you might give to someone dear to you

Already open? Contain before you deepen

This is most useful after you have already opened yourself to a state, through loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, dealing with grief, listening to music, prayer, engagement with erotic energy, exhaustion, or being overwhelmed by beauty. This is to stabilize your state, not to make it stronger.

I already have an open state, now I want to aim that open state and make it stronger.

Look around you, orient yourself to where you are, what date it is. Focus on the physical sensation of squeezing your thumbs against your index fingers, feel the friction.

Now, I will only allow myself to go as far as I can integrate. My body will be safe, my adult self is here, my inner child doesn't have to do this alone.

Now, tell me the next thing I need to know, in symbols, feelings, questions, actions, in doses that I can integrate.

Stay awake when your mind likes to escape

You can do this practice sitting up, with your eyes open, etc.

Begin by saying to yourself that you are not going to go away in this practice, you are coming more.

Then choose an object to look at, or feel your spine, etc.

Ask yourself if your daydreaming is helping you to receive guidance or digest emotional experiences, or if you are escaping from something.

Then you can ask for help to take action based on the guidance or to come into the present moment and see what you are escaping from.

If you find that being still leads you to escape into sleepiness and diffuse states, you can work with increasing alertness rather than relaxation, keep your eyes open and work with doing a movement with your hands, which you repeat for a while and then stop deliberately in order to notice if there is any residual activity.

You can say something like: ‘While you keep your eyes open, press your thumb and forefinger together and then let go; do this a few times, becoming more and more clear and alert each time. Now deliberately stop doing that movement and notice if there is any residual activity or if it has completely stopped.’ Work with a level of alertness that is useful to you.

Then breath and affirm

Sleep induction

Sleep induction has a different job. In inner work, the adult returns, writes, and acts. At bedtime, analysis can remain off duty. Revelation can wait; the task is rest.

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Fractionation is a term for going out and back into a deeper stage of absorption. If you use it openly you need to make it clear that you are using it as that will help you avoid the problem of all answers leading to going deeper.

Open your eyes and come back out to normal awareness. You can choose to stop at this point if you want to. If you want to go deeper then simply close or soften your eyes again and notice the difference. Of course you can stop at this point if you want to.

Deepening, if useful

Remind yourself, 'If this is useful to me in this moment, my attention will become gathered. If this is not useful, I will still be as awake as I need to be.'

Imagine a scene that would help keep up the attention on what is useful to attend to. It could be that of being in a place within the heart, a garden, a temple, near a fire with the Protector nearby, at a lake, or simply being with the adult sitting in a comfortable chair. Create one scene that will be sufficient.

“Who or what needs to speak first?”

Optional trance depth check

And then I simply wait. I give over the responsibility.

If it is useful at this time, my wise subconscious will allow some signal to come through – one finger will begin to twitch, or pulse, or lift, or warm, or tingle, or become noticeable to me in some way, showing that there is now a place for me to meet with it.

I don’t force this, I don’t fake this, I just wait with love and notice.

It may or it may not. But neither proves the truth of it – it may still be listening.

A shortcut back into hypnosis

Learn a Useful Induction and Full Return First, the reason I suggest not to use a short cut is because you should not be in trance when driving. However, I have seen my dad put two fingers in a mudra (like the ok mudra) to help him relax while driving and that is just his experience, it does not mean that you should. However, it is best to have different triggers for different things, so having a different trigger to be calmly alert while driving, and a different one to go into inward hypnosis is a good idea.

Choose a Unique Word, Phrase or Movement You may want to add a gesture, but it's not necessary. When you are in a familiar and welcome hypnotic state that you like - not at the height of an emotional experience, and not in a child state or with a traumatic scene - start to pair that state with that word, phrase or gesture. You are giving that word, phrase or gesture a meaning that you choose.

When you are in a place and time where you have set aside time and it is appropriate and you want to deliberately start hypnosis with your short cut, then you will find yourself in that familiar and welcome state, from where you can change the direction of your experience or end the hypnosis.

Return Fully When at another appropriate time you want to deliberately start practicing hypnosis, use your short cut. You can start to make your longer induction shorter as you find that the short cut works, but if it doesn't work, you can always use the familiar induction. There is no set number of times that you need to do this, or that you need to be instantaneously really deep into hypnosis or experience a particular sensation, it is completely up to you.

First, is it useful? Will it be there when you want it to be, not there when you don't want it to be? Can you change your mind about it and get back when you want to? It shouldn't mean you'll do anything you're told, anytime someone tells you, or even if you hear it overheard. Being able to go in faster should not limit what you can work with.

It's not a good idea to do it while driving or anything where you need to be actively paying attention even if it is open eyed and even if the words are conditional.

When you don't want it any more, stop practicing, take it out of any recordings or active apps you're using, go back to a familiar induction and say you're done using it. If you have problems not being able to stop using it or not being able to come back from it easily, get qualified help. The trigger should only be for the next time you decide you want to do a session, it shouldn't keep you out of line today.

Appendix H: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens”

I’m writing this appendix from a place of experience.

Sometimes, in self-hypnosis, meditation, lucid dreaming, loveyhuasca, periods of grief, prayer, or other altered states of consciousness, people encounter something that isn’t just an emotion, or a young part. It may seem like a demon, jinn, parasitic energy, dark intelligence, terrifying archetypal being, or come as a voice or image of some sort. Whatever it is, it’s unwanted, intrusive, and seemingly full of hate, or seduction, or mockery, or just feels different.

Do I need to provide a guide for what these beings might be? Maybe they are literal beings. Maybe they are a symbolic form the mind creates to hold difficult feelings, past trauma, dissociated energy, or things picked up from parents, partners, or ancestors. It doesn’t matter. The question is:

What is the best way to respond to them, in order to feel safe, clear, loving, grounded, and un-hooked?

Start with the room, the body, and basic safety

Do this when seeing/encountering a demonic/jinn-like or other hostile or intrusive presence: This is a quick reference to the basics of the triage steps, medical danger, environment, body, overload, and mind opened. Open eyes, make sure of environmental safety, feel connection with body such as feet on floor, reduce environmental stimulation, remove yourself from any hostile environments or people, stop doing anything that would increase stimulation to the mind. Do not attempt to go deeper, to find out more, to be ontological, or do anything to increase destabilization.

Mantra: Only what can be integrated is allowed at this time. If it is too much, it can wait. The adult self is always available to be there. Return the body to a safe place.

If at any time during self-hypnosis sessions, if there is danger to yourself or others, if things become too scary and psychosis-like, if unable to sleep, if feeling extremely paranoid, if experiencing chest pain, seizures, serious overheating, drug or other substance overdose, or inability to function, the session is over, and help should be sought in the real world.

A response check, not a verdict about what it is

1. Come into a stable state, if needed put your hand on your heart, etc.

2. Internalize that you do not have to know what this is. Ask yourself if it would be appropriate to send it some warmth or if you need to place a boundary with it. Know that you are under no obligation to do whatever it is asking of you.

3. If you feel vulnerable, tightness in your throat, sadness, fear or you sense you need to protect yourself in some manner, bring in your Nurturer. If it continues to be hostile or you feel afraid, then do not continue to engage with it.

4. Again, you do not have to know where this is coming from. Ask yourself if this way of responding to it seems to be clearing it. It is ok to use a combination of love and boundaries to interact with it.

Do not fight from fear

My first thought is to fight it, banish it, hate it, show it I’m more powerful, argue with it, panic, be it, etc. I have seen different prayers, mantras, protections, banishing and exorcism forms that some people find useful. The problem is, if you fight from fear…

…it becomes the center of your attention and when you hate it, give it a hook in you, or fight it from pride or panic….

“I do not need to hate you. I do not need to become you. I do not need to listen to you. I do not need to fight you from fear. I simply return my attention to loving awareness.”

A bodily boundary: compassion present, door closed

Often when I sense a presence I feel it to be not so good, a little hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, violating. To project soft sentimental mush to it is like inviting it in for tea. Instead use something like this:

Sit up, bring your feet down, lift up with your spine, bring your shoulders back gently, feel the skin boundary of your torso, feel the perimeter of your body, and say:

Even if I sense there is suffering here, which is to be wished well, I am returning all of that to its own space. The skin boundary is where my adult life exists. You may not come into this house.

“Compassion is present. The door is closed.”

If it might be psychosis or destabilization

Do you mean a situation where you're experiecning something symbolically which represents a hostile presence, but you are able to work through to a resolution and end up feeling grounded and loving? Or, do you mean a situation that becomes paranoiac, that persists, that prevents you sleeping, that puts you or others at risk, or that you cannot reality test?

If the latter, you need to get help. If you think you are being attacked over a number of days, if you cannot sleep or function normally, if you are hearing voices or are compelled to harm yourself or others, if you are manic, or unable to communicate, or unable to reality test, you need to get help.

If your practice enhances your sense of love, grounding, relationship, honesty and ability to function in the world, carry on. If your practice enhances feelings of paranoia, inability to sleep, grandiosity, isolation, fear or feelings of unreality, stop and get help.

The cosmic-download humility test

To cut off all contact and communication from “bad” entities, such as from hostile presences, shadow forces, grandiose parts of yourself, or anything which gives you imagery in altered states that you are special or chosen, or that you are being “downloaded” with information, etc. say:

Thank you for the imagery, but unless you can tell me something that will help me do the dishes or clean my room, or some other simple, down-to-earth, everyday task that increases love in my life or in the world, then what you are telling me is not what I need on my path.

I am only interested in guidance that will help me to do everyday tasks in a way that increases beauty, honesty, relating, humility, dependability, and usefulness to others.

Don’t become an entity hobbyist

Now the training to deal with demons, jinn or whatever term the client uses to describe that which the client is trying to deal with is pretty much the same as it would be to deal with any negative presence or what I call Unattached Burdens, so I do not want to turn this into a hobby of entities.

Appendix J: A practical induction library

To use any of these sequences you first read over them, decide if you want to use them and if you do you start working with them. You adapt them to suit the family by using lighter versions, keeping the eyes open or using no trance contact instead of induction if appropriate. Then you see what happens including nothing happening and from that you decide what to do next. Maybe move on to the next part of the sequence, or imagine what you are describing, or use a different sensory channel, or just sit there in silence or maybe stop completely. At the end of each induction you bring the family back up to full waking consciousness.

If the family are having difficulty imagining anything vividly you can translate the metaphors into a different sensory channel or just talk about them, give the rhythm, describe the space, touch the family, move them or just know what you mean.

Stretch and release

Starting Point: Lie on the floor and/or place yourself in a position where you can feel support under one hand or foot. Gently press and/or stretch and then release the area. Note any sensations, or just imagine the press/stretch/release. Repeat with a maximum of three areas. Use the word ‘release’ to guide you. Now move or not – whichever feels most alive. See if you can sense what’s emerging; an area, a voice within. Try to find a way of supporting what wants your attention. When ready, restore movement and return.

Supported floating

Try for a moment to let yourself feel that you are not weighting down upon your support at all, then try feeling as though you were weighting just a tiny bit- only one percent- of the effort onto the support, so that you are almost floating above it. Then try feeling your normal amount of weighting down and pressure upon it. Notice if there are any differences that you feel. (You can try to fractionate this by switching your attention back and forth between the normal weighting and the supported weighting, perhaps on in breaths and out breaths. If you are going to do that, be aware that you are doing it before you begin.) Then you can return back to normal weighting, firmly touching your support, as you choose.

Rhythmic breath or pulse

Try it with a natural rhythm; perhaps the rhythm of breathing or a slight hum in the throat. Try it with a more artificial rhythm, such as tapping a finger or listening to sounds outside. Even try it counting (silently) to yourself, or even with no rhythm at all. Say the words 'here, and here again' over and over, until suddenly, stop the rhythm. This will bring about its own rhythm, the first one that appears - do not try and make it blank. This might bring a bit more clarity to what word, feeling, need or action is coming up. Then go back to using a normal rhythm.

Unwinding object

A quick exercise for when you have several concerns going on. Visualise each one as a strand of yarn, or even better, have some by you to help. When you've placed them all, take a minute to look at them all (without changing them, though you could label them if needed, by saying a word or two). How many did you end up with? Now pick one that is important to do something about, put the others somewhere you can see them, and come back to this page.

Sensory journey

Ground yourself in your current physical space by noticing the acoustics of the room and sensing your body. Visualize stepping purposefully toward your chosen location. As you "walk," focus your attention by gathering information about the surroundings through auditory and tactile senses, such as listening to your footsteps, feeling textures, or observing landmarks. You may skip this step and jump straight into a dialogue if preferred, or change the scenery. Remember, there's no hidden meaning to look for, just allow the scene to unfold naturally and let curiosity guide you to discover who or what you need to speak to. Once you've completed your interaction, retrace your steps back to your starting point and close the space.

Gradual wave

Begin with the smallest area possible that is neutral. Sense the current condition and sense it radiating outward to the next area, which should still feel comfortable. Continue this, pausing and sensing in each new area, or continue with the original area, only. Sense what the body needs to feel better, without thinking of medical terms. Allow the image to fade, sense the whole body, the contact points, and repeat the process.

Care workshop

First get ready as if you were going to work with a patient. Time, place, tools and boundaries. When you invite them in, the signal, the feeling or the younger state to come as close as you want them to be. Be careful to not use language which makes you fragmented. Ask them what they need, wait and see if you want to reconnect with them. If not, rest and see again. If you have an adult part which can do this or borrow a function from someone else, speak to them. You decide the words, the pace and what you want to do. The goal is to be as good as you can and not erase your history. Finally, close as you would with a patient. Say that you are whole, an adult and come back.

Resource embodiment

Choose someone or something who has a characteristic you want to adopt. Close your eyes and imagine them. Now imagine yourself becoming them, standing, walking and talking like them, just 1% more, or if you are uncomfortable with this, simply observe them, but in either case be aware of how you now have more access to that quality. Notice what happens. Repeat a few times. Now think of a situation you want to use that characteristic in. Finally let go of the person/thing, but keep the characteristic, and say to yourself "I am me", and notice how you have increased access to the characteristic you wanted.

No-trance inner contact

Things to do in between: keep the eyes open, notice where the practice is taking place and on what day, notice the feet, read something, write something, notice that one is still relatively normally aware.

Invitation: choose a question and keep it in mind, do not specifically focus or narrow the awareness further.

Choice: do whatever comes to mind, answer the question or write it down, write that one does not know, rest, change the question, ask someone else, stop the practice, etc.

Autonomous signal: write anything that comes to mind, no interpretation.

Deepener: none, it is not necessary to reach a state that is less alert.

Other autonomous: have the adult part of yourself answer the question in any way, preferably in writing or by taking an action.

Integration/exit: reality test the autonomous signal and take an action based on that, end the practice (no special exit is needed since no state was achieved that one needs to exit from).

Appendix B: NLP without turning yourself into a sales seminar

You don’t have to know the terms to use the system. If you want to brush up on the art of imagery, how imagery is linked to bodily states, how to effectively rehearse new behaviors, how to choose more effective sentences to say to yourself, etc., then you might want to read this appendix. If you don’t know a little bit about NLP, it’s easy to turn NLP into a bag of tricks and forget that love, truth, contact, and consent are essential.

The four NLP layers

When it works, it works on a Sensory Level of NLP: changing where people see or hear an image, the distance or size or brightness, the volume of a sound, the posture of a remembered person, the pressure of an unpleasant sensation.

Second, it works on a State Level of NLP: helping them to access warmth, or a feeling of adult-ness, or courage, or steadiness, or love, or clarity.

Third, it works on a Strategy level of NLP: helping people to practice a new strategy.

Fourth, it works on a Language Level of NLP: pacing what is there, opening up people’s awareness, presuming their ability to do something safe, linking cause and effect in new ways, embedding suggestions, or asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative, or grandiose language.

The Milton Model, minus the covert sales seminar

It's called the Milton Model and has to do with the architecture of the sentence. When I say "Relax now", or "Stop being anxious", or even "Trust me" a part of me braces against it.

The idea is to use indirect language to get past the part that wants to argue with me, and get to the place I want to go to.

To do that, I start with something I know to be true, and I take the pressure off by presuming the least possible capacity in the person and invite just one movement:

"As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone."

That way I pace reality, I open up awareness, I validate the function of what I'm doing, I presuppose the capacity to do what I want, I use a bridge to make the link easier, I invite only one small movement, and I have a way of testing with the body if it's happening.

Pattern 10: Meta Model questions — the de-hypnosis tool

To ‘Milton Model’ is to open things up. To ‘Meta Model’ is to ask “What do yo mean by that?” In order to be truly effective (and ethical) with people, it is necessary to do both.

“What do yo mean ‘Specifically’? According to who? ‘Good’ compared to what? ‘Always’? ‘Never’? What specifically would happen? How do yo know? What would constitute proof for ya?”

If, in session, it feels like the body is stiffening up, ‘Milton’ it. If it feels like truth is eluding ya, ‘Meta’ it.

Anchoring — giving the body a doorway back

An anchor is a cue that triggers a state. It can be anything - putting your hand on your heart, touching two fingers together, taking a breath, saying a word, a particular posture, scent, song, and so on. Choose something, then find a real state to anchor it to. When you're clearly in the state, apply the anchor and say, 'This is available' . (If you're using the anchor to get back into hypnosis, find a nice useful state - you don't need to be at the peak of emotion, just in a nice receptive state. For more about that, see 'A shortcut back into hypnosis' in the main induction section. ) Make sure you also have a way to bring yourself back to a nice, calming, alert state when you want to be fully awake (see 'synchronicity' above for a way of doing that).

Using synchronicity as your own wake-up bell

Sometimes when my clients notice a synchronicity they are asking straight way what it means. Sometimes it does give them a very good insight, sometimes it gives them a reason to start obsessing and look for patterns in everything. I am using noticing a synchronicity in a different way. I am using it as a signal to WAKE UP.

It is my cue to:

Whenever I notice a synchronicity, I use it to wake up in whatever state I am in at that moment, feel my body, the room I am in and go to the highest state I can where I can objectively and clearly see the situation I am in from the highest possible perspective, feeling my body and being still within the human reality. From this place I feel whatever feelings, search for the truth of the situation, and if I am in a negative state, I check if there is a message of my Inner Child, Protector, if I need to go through some grieving, if there is a message of my physical body about some problem that needs solving, or if there is a need for me to take some action in this situation. From this place of clarity and peace I am free to choose what to do next and usually I can do at least one thing that comes from a loving place. In this state I am also free and joyful and I feel grateful.

In short it is my cue to: Stop-orient-go wider-reality check-listen-do at least one thing from a loving place.

It enables me to not get into identification, but still hear the message of the state if it is a negative one.

Installing the synchronicity cue

Mentally rehearse: when next synchronicity noticed (even harmless ones count),

feel 'whoa' as attention stimulated,

feel feet/body/breath/room to stimulate re-embodiment,

reiterate to yourself "when I notice synchronicity, it is a bell to wake me up, not a message to heed",

optionally ask Nurturer/Protector/Leader their thoughts,

rehearse further steps to get a more grounded and wide view,

rehearse what additional action to take, and finally rehearse waking completely,

Mind the caveats : it must be self-authored, obviously under control, reversible, and restricted to just helping orientation. It must not be used for decision-making, intuition, inhibition, or otherwise be under someone else's control.

This is a kind of implementation intention , for which there is evidence of efficacy (a good starting point is this paper by Gollwitzer ). Note that this specific application of implementation intentions probably hasn't been studied.

Synchronicity cues, like any cue, run the risk of creating false positives because you are creating an association in your mind by rehearsing it (this is the same mechanism by which synchronicity cues work), and when you are absorbed and/or destabilized, your mind may look for that pattern and interpret it as present when it may not actually be. Research has shown that people that score highly on apophenia (the tendency to perceive meaningful patterns where none exists) also score highly on false positives for patterns that are not present, and also score highly on traits on the psychosis spectrum (Blain et al., Grant et al.).

If you feel that synchronicity cues are creating false positives (you find yourself compelled to scan your environment for them, you are unable to sleep, you are anxious, you feel that random events are occurring to communicate something to you specifically, you find yourself unable to tell if they are real or not, etc.), you should deactivate them.

You can do this by simply ceasing to rehearse them, and saying, while fully awake, “Synchronicity is no longer to be used as a cue, and I let it go.” Also remove it from your list of cues so that you stop rehearsing it.

Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

When I reframe something that is dishonest with myself in the process, I’m no better off than before, so I have to be honest when I reframe. To reframe in a helpful way is to ask myself a series of questions like: “What else could be true here?” or “What is this part trying to do for me?” or “How would my Nurturer reframe this?” or “How would my Protector reframe this?” or “How would my Leader reframe this?” and so on.

Perceptual positions — self, other, witness, universal heart

1. How do I feel about this from inside myself? 2. If I were inside of this other person (or tree, or dog or whatever is not-you), how might I feel? 3. If I were across the room watching this, what would I see? 4. From the universal heart, what might be true, loving, clear about boundaries, and good for everyone involved?

Yes, it’s possible to use these positions to let yourself off the hook. It’s also possible to use them to get off the hook! Use them to see the truth from more than one angle. They’re a great way to get out of a prison of perception.

Future pacing — let the future test the insight

Don’t end with “I understand.” Ask where life will test the understanding, picture the actual cue, and rehearse the smallest better response.

“If [cue], then I [small action].”

The Swish, softened

In classic NLP, one of the uses of the Swish was to replace an old image of yourself with a new, better one. Some people find that method jarring. So here is a gentler way to do it, leaving the old pattern in place, but letting it sit side by side with a new pattern, so that the client can feel, in their body, which one they want to pursue, and see what it would take to get there.

Parts integration, without pretending the conflict is solved

“What does one side want?” “What does the other side fear?” “What need sits under both?” “What third option honors both without letting either run the whole life?”

Running the whole NLP sequence

Induce or contain (if client already in altered state).

Ask permission to work with this part.

Help client accurately represent this pattern. What does it look like? Where? How big? How close? What color? How does it move?

Ask what it is trying to do for the client.

Have client make adaptive changes in the pattern (move it further away, turn down the volume, change body posture, slow it down, etc.).

Introduce the three new adults (Nurturer, Protector and Leader) and have them interact with the pattern in new ways.

Have client anchor the new state (heart, fingers, breath, body posture, etc.).

Have client future pace into a situation where this pattern used to be triggered, but now he/she will perform a new behavior.

Test and retest to ensure that new pattern is useful and that you have supporting evidence for your interpretation of the situation.

Help client exit altered state and perform a normal behavior.
